hypotheses.mechanism: The end->start stitch (re-add the ILP's own edge between a track end at t and a track start at t+1 that the motion relink left unlinked) gave +0.0020 on CONFIRMATION on top of the edge filter but was rejected because 44b6 'gains on only 15% of videos'. I recomputed the per-video deltas (l6_stitch/per_video_confirmation.csv, ef_st_all vs ef_a3_rl_pr): 44b6 = 11 wins / 1 loss / 59 exact ties (worst loss -0.0012); 6bba = 46 wins / 0 losses / 18 ties. So it did not fail on harm. It failed because 44b6 label coverage is 0.2-1.3%, so most 44b6 videos contain no evaluable stitched pair and must tie. On the non-tied videos the sign test gives 11/12 (one-sided p ~0.003) on 44b6 and 46/46 on 6bba: the most embryo-consistent change we have measured. Transfer margin: the added edges are ILP edges with local precision 0.934 (0.967 at p>=0.7, 240 TP / 8 FP for st_p07). Break-even precision for an added edge is J/(1+J) ~0.474, so the rule stays positive on an unseen embryo even if out-of-sample precision halves. It adds no nodes, so the node multiplier is unchanged and the whole gain is edge J, which avoids the node-deletion trap that sank min-track-length (+0.013 offline, -0.004 public).
hypotheses.change: Selection-protocol fix plus shipping. (1) Replace the per-embryo '>= 55% of videos gain' criterion with a tie-aware one: wins/(wins+losses) >= 0.7 on non-tied videos per embryo, plus the existing mean and CI gates. (2) Ship stitch_final_graph (tools/build_probe_kernel.py --patch stitch) at the end of the tail, after the edge filter and before the short-track filter and linefit, in its conservative form st_p07: add the ILP edge u->v only if u is a track end at t, v is a track start at t+1, the ILP had selected u->v with edge_prob >= 0.7, neither node is on a fork, and each node gets at most one added edge. If probe 29 shows the edge filter does not transfer, re-measure the stitch on the exp48 base without ef before bundling.
hypotheses.upper_bound: The FN anatomy puts the track-break oracle (b_break, 399 FN) at +0.003. st_all already gets +0.0020 on confirmation (281 TP / 19 FP added), so the remaining headroom in this class is <= +0.001. At the out-of-sample worst case (precision 0.47) the gain is ~0.
hypotheses.lab_test: Kaggle CPU lab, exp48 base (leaf prune 0.3 + DaughterNet insertion) with and without ef, stitch st_p07 and st_all, all 199 videos. Report per embryo: mean delta, 90% CI, and wins/losses/ties. Success: confirmation delta >= +0.0015, wins/(wins+losses) >= 0.8 on both embryos, node ratio unchanged (+-0.01%). Then it goes into the bundle probe, not a solo probe, because +0.002 is below the LB noise floor.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Local +0.0015..+0.0020 (measured +0.00179 for st_p07 and +0.00211 for st_all on confirmation). Public/private +0.001..+0.002 if ILP-edge precision stays >= 0.8 out of sample: 0.002 x (0.8-0.47)/(0.93-0.47) ~ +0.0014 at the pessimistic end.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Low to moderate. The ILP edge choice is in-sample (edge net trained on all 199 videos), but the precision margin is ~2x break-even. Node count is untouched. The known failure mode (a relink-stage change like relink-off losing 0.002 on the LB) does not apply: this removes no edges and re-adds only pairs the relink left open.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: Stitching was never closed. It was set aside only by the per-embryo 55%-of-videos gate, and I show that gate is mis-specified for a 0.2-1.3%-coverage embryo (59/71 exact ties, 1 loss). It is not a relink knob or gap-filler variant: it runs after the relink, adds no nodes, and uses only the ILP's own edges.

hypotheses.mechanism: The division term is where public and private differ most, and our aggressiveness knobs were tuned against the public number. Public division Jaccard is 0.36 (probe 26: 0.947 -> 0.911 with zero forks). Both train embryos score far lower on the official metric: exp39 44b6 5/10/21 = 0.139, 6bba 18/33/107 = 0.114. The public value most likely comes from one embryo with few GT divisions (+-0.04 rounding alone; with ~10 GT divisions the sampling SD of J is ~0.1). An added fork with evaluable precision p raises division J iff p > J/(1+J). Break-even is 0.265 at the public J but only 0.10-0.12 at the train-embryo J, which is the better prior for the 71% private embryos. DaughterNet v1 steal insertion (cap 4) has evaluable precision 4/15 = 0.27: a tie on public (probe 28, +0.001) but clearly positive at J ~0.13. The cap was selected on a small 64-video SELECTION set (the binding constraint was cap 4 per video; thresholds 0.05-0.3 did not bind) and judged against a public-derived precision floor of 0.31. Private-optimal aggressiveness is higher: any insertion rank whose marginal precision exceeds ~0.17 (break-even at J 0.14 plus a 0.05 margin) should be kept.
hypotheses.change: In the DaughterNet insertion stage (tools/div_insert.py / --patch divinsert, after the tail), keep the ensemble threshold 0.4 and alpha 1. Choose the per-video cap by marginal evaluable precision on all 199 videos (OOF p from the 5-fold leak-group split), with a precision floor of 0.17 instead of the public-derived 0.31. Candidate caps are 4, 6, 8 and 12, with steals on. Also scale the cap with the number of tracks alive in the video (cap = ceil(k x n_tracks/median_n_tracks)), so denser private embryos with more real mitoses are not starved by a flat per-video count. Ship it only in the second, private-leaning final (see finals-emax-diversify).
hypotheses.upper_bound: Reach: 62/151 GT parents are exact-frame candidates in the pool, 23 are already TP. If raising the cap adds 20 TP at marginal precision 0.27 (54 FP), local J goes from 23/(23+43+128) = 0.119 to 43/(43+97+108) = 0.173, i.e. +0.0054 in score. Realistically about a third of that: +0.0015..+0.002.
hypotheses.lab_test: Kaggle CPU lab, exp48 base (+ef if probe 29 holds), caps 4, 6, 8, 12 and track-scaled k, all 199 videos with OOF p. Log added evaluable TP/FP per cap increment, per embryo. Compute score under three division-J scenarios by reweighting the division term: local (0.13), mid (0.25) and public (0.36). Success: cap c* has marginal precision >= 0.17 on both embryos, local delta vs cap 4 >= +0.001, and a public-scenario loss <= 0.0005.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Private +0.001..+0.002. Each extra evaluable fork at p = 0.25 and J = 0.14 adds (0.25 x 1.14 - 0.14)/D ~ 0.0011 J with D ~ 130 per 135 videos. About 3% of insertions are evaluable (15 of 466), so cap 4 -> 8 adds ~13-15 evaluable forks, giving +0.015 J = +0.0015 score. Public: -0.0005..+0.0003, since marginal p ~0.25 is at the public break-even.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Moderate. DaughterNet p is honestly OOF (5 folds with 44b6 leak groups), so the precision estimate is not in-sample. But the insertion edges and steals act on an in-sample graph, and pool precision (parent AUC 0.875 on the pool) may drop on new embryos. The bet is asymmetric: at worst about -0.0005 on the public-like embryo, and +0.002 if private division J resembles the train embryos.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: The closed items are the DivNet veto and the division pair model (B32). This is the already-shipped DaughterNet insertion from probe 28, re-tuned for a different target: a J-aware precision floor based on the train-embryo division J instead of the public J, with the cap chosen on all 199 videos. No new model.

hypotheses.mechanism: Kaggle ranks each team by the better private score of its 2 selected finals, so the pair should maximise E[max(X1,X2)], not two near-copies of the best public score. For D = X2 - X1 ~ N(mu, sigma) on private, E[max] = E[X1] + mu*Phi(mu/sigma) + sigma*phi(mu/sigma). Private is ~71% of test and comes from other embryos. Public is one embryo whose own measurements are volatile: identical notebooks vary by +-0.003, the division J of 0.36 is small-n, and in-sample lab gains flip sign on the LB. Our lab shows which changes are embryo-consistent. Edge filter: 44b6 43/14/14 and 6bba 51/4/9 wins/losses/ties, gain J-driven, node ratio 0.99958, so the multiplier share is ~0.00004 of +0.016. Stitch: 11/1/59 and 46/0/18. Division cap: private-leaning by construction. Putting these private-leaning components in F2, on top of a public-proven F1, captures their upside without betting the only counted score on them.
hypotheses.change: Final-selection rule (by 29 Sep 20:00 UTC). F1 = the 'public-proven' stack: exp48 + coordhead port (+ edge filter only if probe 29 >= 0.950). F2 = F1 + every component that passes the per-embryo lab gates, uses the tie-aware sign test, is J-driven (multiplier share < 30%) and has a public probe no worse than F1 - 0.003. Candidates: edge filter if probe 29 was a tie, stitch st_p07, DaughterNet cap c*, leaf prune. Never choose F2 as the max public score over several near-identical variants. The pseudo-private resampling below also ranks the components; one whose resampled D has P(D<0) > 0.3 goes to neither final.
hypotheses.upper_bound: For F2 - F1 on private with mu = +0.002 and sigma = 0.004: E[max] - E[F1] = 0.002 x Phi(0.5) + 0.004 x phi(0.5) = 0.00138 + 0.00141 = +0.0028. Picking only F2 would give +0.002 and two near-copies about +0.0002. The diversification premium over the best single choice is ~+0.0008, bounded by sigma/sqrt(2*pi) ~0.0016 at mu = 0.
hypotheses.lab_test: Pseudo-private resampling on the Kaggle CPU lab outputs, no new pipeline runs. Draw 2,000 'embryo-like' test sets: a bootstrap over the 11 44b6 leak groups and over 6bba videos in contiguous blocks, mixed 29/71 like public/private. Compute the distribution of D for each candidate (F1, F2) pair and pick the pair that maximises mean max(X1, X2), subject to F2's public probe >= F1 - 0.003. Success: the chosen pair's resampled E[max] exceeds the best single final's by >= +0.0005, with P(F2 < F1) <= 0.35.
hypotheses.expected_gain: +0.0005..+0.0015 of expected private score over selecting the two highest public submissions (from the E[max] arithmetic above with sigma 0.002-0.004). The larger benefit is avoiding a -0.003..-0.005 private loss from a single public-overfit choice.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: None to the pipeline. The risk is in the inputs: lab D estimates are optimistic for network-trusting components (in-sample edge net), so sigma is under-estimated. Mitigate by inflating lab sigma by 1.5x and requiring every F2 component's public probe to be no worse than -0.003.
hypotheses.not_closed_because: Final selection has not been tested or closed. CONTEXT §11a only says never to pick finals by max public score. This makes it a quantitative E[max] rule with a per-embryo, J-vs-multiplier and tie-aware component screen.

hypotheses.mechanism: x138's +0.007 comes from sub-voxel coordinates. Part of it needs no learning: integer-voxel peaks at z spacing 1.625 um carry a uniform rounding error of up to +-0.81 um (RMS 0.47 um in z, 0.12 um per xy axis), which enters every relink, gap and division gate and the scorer's Hungarian matching. The V1284 head removes that rounding and also learns a residual from frozen UNet features of the two train embryos. Those features are in-sample: the detector saw all 199 videos, and LOEO recall drops from 0.94 to 0.85 on an unseen embryo. The known annotation offset (dz ~ -0.57 um) is also embryo-dependent, so the learned part is the component most likely to behave differently on private embryos. A label-free sub-voxel estimate from the detector's own peak shape transfers identically to any embryo: a 3-point parabola per axis on the logit of the fused heatmap (probabilities saturate at ~0.999, so fitting on p would be flat). Used as a guard, it keeps the head's shift where the two agree and falls back to the label-free estimate where the head extrapolates.
hypotheses.change: In predict_unet_transformer.py, at peak extraction (after the 3 um max-pool NMS on the fused 8-view/2-seed heatmap, before the int16 cast that the coordhead patch removes): for each peak, read the 3x3x3 logit patch and compute delta_a = 0.5*(l[-1]-l[+1])/(l[-1]-2*l[0]+l[+1]) per axis, clamped to +-0.5 voxel. Convert to um with the (1.625, 0.40625, 0.40625) scale, adjusted if the heatmap grid is downsampled (the model returns a downsample tuple, default (1,4,4); check the heatmap resolution). With the V1284 head: final = head shift if |head - parabola| <= 1.0 um per axis, else the parabola shift. Without the head, the parabola shift alone. Feed the float coords into the same trilinear feature gather and float-coordinate path as the coordhead port.
hypotheses.upper_bound: If the mean matched centre error is ~1.8 um RMS, removing the rounding alone gives sqrt(1.8^2 - 0.47^2) = 1.74 um (-3.5%), about a third of the head's reported -10.4%. Standalone ceiling ~1/3 x 0.007 = +0.0025. Added to the head, the guard only changes nodes where the two disagree by more than 1 um: +0.000..+0.001 expected, plus protection against a private embryo where the head's learned residual turns harmful (bounded by the head's own +0.007).
hypotheses.lab_test: One Kaggle GPU capture pass (~1-2 GPU h) on 40 train videos (20 per embryo, 44b6 leak groups kept whole). Dump coords, V1284 features and 3x3x3 logit patches per peak. On CPU: match to GT within 4 um and report mean and 90th-percentile centre error per embryo for int / parabola / public head / guarded blend. Transfer check: fit a ridge copy of the head on 6bba-only captures, evaluate on 44b6 and vice versa, and compare the cross-embryo error increase with the parabola's (zero by construction). Success: parabola error <= int - 3% on both embryos, and the guarded blend <= head on both. Then a post-hoc official-metric replay shifting detector-origin nodes (node count fixed, so any gain is J), and one LB probe of exp48 + coordhead + guard vs exp48 + coordhead.
hypotheses.expected_gain: Public +0.000..+0.001 on top of the coordhead port, private +0.000..+0.002 (variance reduction). Standalone, if the head fails to port: +0.001..+0.0025.
hypotheses.transfer_risk: Low. The rule has no trained parameters and does not change node count. Risks: heatmap saturation (use logits, and skip peaks whose curvature is >= 0, i.e. not a strict maximum), a downsampled heatmap grid, and the 8-view TTA average flattening peaks, which biases the parabola toward 0 (conservative).
hypotheses.not_closed_because: The closed lines are TTA variants and detector fine-tunes. This is a deterministic sub-voxel post-step on the existing heatmap and an embryo-invariant guard for the head being ported, which the brief invites ('ideas that build on sub-voxel coordinates are welcome'). It is not the port itself.
